deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is Gauss's first absolute-intensity campaign at Göttingen, 30 April 1832. It is the experimental basis of 'Intensitas vis magneticae terrestris ad mensuram absolutam revocata' (read 15 Dec 1832, printed 1833). The page has two parts: (I) the magnetic meridian found by theodolite plus mirror and scale; (II) the vibration period of needle A loaded with two 100 g weights.

PART I. Meridian.
The theodolite in the 'Winterzimmer' is levelled. Its circle reading on the azimuth mark (Jäger's Gartenhaus) is 224°40'32.25". A mirror is fixed to needle A. Through the theodolite telescope Gauss reads the image of a millimetre scale reflected in that mirror, with mark A and the 'correction' (collimation adjustment) underneath. The readings are:
- 224°1'26.25" → 271.5
- 224°20'32.25" → 227.8
- 223°41'57.50" → 313.95
- 224°3'30.00" → 265.9
The plumb line from the theodolite axis falls at scale point 254.0.

Scale value (my reconstruction of the arithmetic): use the two extreme settings. The angle difference is 224°20'32.25" - 223°41'57.50" = 38'34.75" = 2314.75". The scale difference is 313.95 - 227.8 = 86.15 divisions. So one division = 2314.75/86.15 = 26.8688", which Gauss writes as 26".868.

Effective distance: the angle of one division is ε = 26.868"/206264.8 = 1.3026e-4 rad. Then D = 1 mm / tan ε = 7676.9 mm. Gauss writes 'Dist. 7m677' and log D = 3.88519. This is the distance from the theodolite to the mirror image of the scale.

Note on the four points: the two intermediate settings are not consistent with this value. They give 1146"/43.7 = 26.22"/div and 1168.75"/42.45 = 27.53"/div. Gauss used only the end points.

Needle reversal: the needle is turned over (A and correction now on top). With the theodolite unchanged at 224°3'30", the reading is 286.1 instead of 265.9. The mean, (265.9 + 286.1)/2 = 276.0, belongs to the magnetic axis, so the mirror/axis collimation error is eliminated.

The theodolite looks along the mirror normal (magnetic meridian) when it sees the plumb point 254.0. Readings decrease as the circle reading increases. Hence the theodolite must be turned forward by (276.0 - 254.0) × 26.868" = 22.0 × 26.868" = 591.10" = 9'51.10".

Result: magnetic meridian = 224°3'30" + 9'51.10" = 224°13'21.10", exactly as Gauss writes.

Implied but not written (mine): the mark lies 224°40'32.25" - 224°13'21.10" = 27'11.15" from the magnetic meridian, which is the ingredient for declination.

PART II. Period with weights at distance 229.25 mm.
Two 100 g weights are hung symmetrically, 229.25 mm apart, so r1 = 114.625 mm from the suspension axis. The needle is in its first position.

Passages of the oscillation number n are timed on the chronometer as t_n. Each is reduced by the provisional period: t_n - 26.40·n gives the epoch of oscillation 0, i.e. 22h29'43.xx". All twelve reductions check:
- n = 1, 2, 3, 4: 43.50, 43.45, 43.35, 43.35
- n = 26, 27, 28: 43.25, 43.25, 43.30
- n = 50, 51, 52: 43.48, 43.50, 43.60
- n = 57, 58: 43.66, 43.66

Group means:
- n = 2½: 43.4125 (43.41)
- n = 27: 43.267 (43.27)
- n = 51: 43.527 (43.53)
- n = 57½ (written '57'): 43.66

The drift of the reduced epoch gives the correction to 26.40. Gauss's result is T1 = 26".4045. It is reproduced exactly by first and last groups only: (43.66 - 43.4125)/(57.5 - 2.5) = 0.2475/55 = 0.0045, so T1 = 26.4045 s. The next page's value 21".1627 is obtained the same way, from groups 2 and 80: (51.1733 - 50.9633)/78 = 0.00269. The middle groups serve only as a check.

Right column, for n = 6–9, 28–29, 54–55: 'Nullpunkt' is the rest point computed from successive elongations (about 305) and 'Schwingung' is the arc in scale divisions (about 312–335). These are needed for the reduction of the period to infinitely small arcs.

Purpose (mine, from the next page and Intensitas): the next page repeats the timing with the weights 39.025 mm apart (r2 = 19.5125 mm), giving T2 = 21.1627 s. From T^2 = π^2 (K + 2p r^2 + k)/(mT) for both loadings one gets mT = 2pπ^2 (r1^2 - r2^2)/(T1^2 - T2^2). This eliminates the unknown moment of inertia K of the needle. The product mT is combined with the deflection experiment (which gives m/T) for the absolute intensity.
errors: No arithmetic errors: all reduced epochs, group means, the scale value 26.868", the distance 7677 mm (log 3.88519) and the meridian reading 224°13'21.10" check.
The index of the last group is written '57' although the mean of oscillations 57 and 58 is 57½; the result 26.4045 requires the interval 55 = 57.5 - 2.5, so this is only a labelling slip.

The period is taken from first and last groups only, not a least-squares fit. A least-squares line through all four group means gives 26.40467 s instead of 26.4045 s, a difference of about 0.00017 s, which is negligible at this precision.

The intermediate theodolite settings imply 26.22" and 27.53" per division, inconsistent with the end-point value 26.868". This points to reading error or scale irregularity; Gauss silently uses the extremes.

The middle group (n = 27) gives a smaller reduced epoch than the first group (43.27 vs 43.41), i.e. the reduced epochs are not monotonic. This reflects timing or declination noise and is not commented on.

The arc column rises from 320.5 (n = 9) to 335.0 (n = 28), which is odd for freely decaying oscillations. It is probably a reading or recording issue, or a disturbance, and is not explained on the page.

results.what: Determination of the magnetic meridian by theodolite and mirror-and-scale reading, with needle reversal to eliminate mirror collimation and conversion of scale divisions to arc via a calibrated scale value
results.modern_name: Mirror-and-scale (Poggendorff–Gauss) optical lever; reversal method for collimation error
results.usually_credited_to: Poggendorff (1826) for mirror reading; Gauss (1832) for the precision theodolite-scale magnetometer

results.what: Reduction of transit times by a provisional period and correction of the period from the drift of the reduced epochs (method of coincident reductions)
results.modern_name: Linear fit of oscillation epochs / period determination by reduced transit times

results.what: Timing the needle loaded with known masses at two different distances to eliminate the unknown moment of inertia in T^2 = π^2 K/(mT)
results.modern_name: Gauss's method for the absolute measurement of the geomagnetic field (moment-of-inertia elimination by added masses)

deep.surprise_reason: These are raw laboratory protocols of Gauss's famous 1832 absolute-intensity experiment, whose method and much of whose data appear in Intensitas (1833). The notebook adds procedural detail, such as the end-point-only period computation and the scale calibration, but nothing new conceptually.

checkable.asserts: Scale value ≈ 26.8688 arcsec per division (from 38'34.75" over 313.95-227.8 divisions)
log10 of effective distance in mm ≈ 3.88519 (distance ≈ 7677 mm)
Mean reading minus plumb point = 22.0 divisions
Corrected period = 26.4045 s exactly from first and last groups
Next-page analogue: corrected period ≈ 21.1627 s by the same first/last method
Implied mT ≈ 1.010e8 (mg, mm, s units) before corrections for arc, torsion and the weights' own moments (context, not on the page)

transcription_corrections: First theodolite reading: the digit was overwritten (214→224); read 224°40'32.25".
'Hierauf die Nadel umgewandt daß A und Correction oben' is correct; the abbreviation is 'u.' / 'und'.
In the summary 'Also', the fourth group index '57' corresponds to the mean of oscillations 57 and 58 (57½).
'(= 26"868)' is the arc value of one scale division; 'giebt Dist. 7m677' with 'log. 3.88519' is log10 of 7677 mm.
'Nullpkt' / 'Schwingg' = Nullpunkt (rest point) and Schwingungsbogen (arc), in scale divisions.
